extracted.intended_audience: American colonists; general public; colonial leaders considering independence
extracted.subtask_description: A political pamphlet arguing for American independence and proposing principles and specific structures for a continental government and charter. Includes rhetorical guidance, reasons to separate from Britain, and concrete proposals for representation and constitutional arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain style and mode of argument
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the following pages I offer nothing more than simple facts, plain arguments, and common sense;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author insists on using simple facts, plain arguments, and common sense; asks reader to "divest himself of prejudice and prepossession, and suffer his reason and his feelings to determine for themselves;" avoid sophistry and appeal to honest plain reasoning rather than rhetorical artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divest prejudice before judging arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: "that he will divest himself of prejudice and prepossession, and suffer his reason and his feelings to determine for themselves;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader should remove prior biases to fairly assess the case for independence; an explicit engagement-condition for taking the pamphlet's arguments seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republican virtue over monarchical corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: The republican part of the constitution (liberty of choosing a house of commons) is the part to glory in; monarchy poisons the republic by engrossing places and swallowing up the power of the commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government should emphasize republican institutions and guard against crown influence (appointments, patronage) which 'hath so effectually swallowed up the power, and eaten out the virtue of the house of commons.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Act promptly — the moment for continental union is now
rubrics_metrics.description: "The sun never shined on a cause of greater worth... Now is the seed time of continental union... The least fracture now will be like a name engraved with the point of a pin on the tender rind of a young oak; the wound will enlarge with the tree, and posterity read it in full grown characters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay risks permanent, growing harm; the present moment is decisive and must be seized — proposals and plans prior to hostilities are superseded ('like the almanacks of the last year').

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation to avoid entanglement in European wars
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission to, or dependence on Great-Britain, tends directly to involve this continent in European wars and quarrels; America should 'steer clear of European contentions, which she never can do, while by her dependence on Britain, she is made the make-weight in the scale of British politics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is advocated as a practical policy to keep American trade and peace intact; commerce will secure friendship and neutrality with Europe only if America is not tied to British foreign policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form governments suited to the continent's scale (not island rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small islands not capable of protecting themselves are proper objects for kingdoms; 'there is something very absurd, in supposing a continent to be perpetually governed by an island.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional arrangements must reflect geographic and political realities — an island (Britain) governing a continent (America) reverses natural order and is impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies should be annual with a single President
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let the assemblies be annual, with a President only."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes frequent (annual) legislative sessions and a singular presiding officer rather than multiple executives or long terms—emphasis on accountability and regular refreshment of mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: More equal representation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should be made more equal among the people/constituents (no further specification here, but presented as a core principle for the assemblies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of powers: domestic business subject to Continental Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: "Their business wholly domestic, and subject to the authority of a Continental Congress."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic matters handled by assemblies should be coordinated under a Continental Congress — implies a delineation of domestic vs continental responsibilities and a continental supremacy for overarching domestic coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-based delegate representation and minimum delegation size
rubrics_metrics.description: "Let each colony be divided into six, eight, or ten, convenient districts, each district to send a proper number of delegates to Congress, so that each colony send at least thirty. The whole number in Congress will be at least 390."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes dividing colonies into multiple districts to elect delegates, with a floor of at least thirty delegates per colony and a Congress size of at least 390 — emphasis on broad, territorial representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation-by-lot for presidential eligibility and ballot election
rubrics_metrics.description: "When the delegates are met, let a colony be taken from the whole thirteen colonies by lot, after which, let the whole Congress choose (by ballot) a president from out of the delegates of that province. In the next Congress, let a colony be taken by lot from twelve only... and so proceeding on till the whole thirteen shall have had their proper rotation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A system designed to rotate the pool from which the president is chosen so that all colonies share opportunity; president chosen by ballot from delegates of the selected colony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supermajority threshold for laws
rubrics_metrics.description: "In order that nothing may pass into a law but what is satisfactorily just, not less than three fifths of the Congress to be called a majority."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires at least three-fifths of Congress for passage of laws — a higher-than-simple-majority threshold to ensure broad consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continental Conference composition
rubrics_metrics.description: "A committee of twenty-six members of Congress, viz. two for each colony. Two members from each House of Assembly, or Provincial Convention; and five representatives of the people at large, to be chosen in the capital city or town of each province..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mixed body combining Congressional experience, provincial assembly members, and representatives elected at large — intended to unite 'knowledge and power' and provide a broadly authorized intermediary to frame a charter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame a Continental Charter (Magna Charta of the Colonies) with specific content
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference's business: 'to frame a Continental Charter, or Charter of the United Colonies... fixing the number and manner of choosing members of Congress, members of Assembly, with their date of sitting, and drawing the line of business and jurisdiction between them... Securing freedom and property to all men, and above all things, the free exercise of religion, according to the dictates of conscience; with such other matter as is necessary for a charter to contain.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charter should (1) fix representation rules and legislative calendars, (2) delineate jurisdictions between continental and provincial bodies, (3) secure freedom and property, and (4) guarantee free exercise of religion — presented as foundational elements of the new constitutional instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolve provisional conference after charter and institute charter-based bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: "Immediately after which, the said Conference to dissolve, and the bodies which shall be chosen conformable to the said charter, to be the legislators and governors of this continent for the time being."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a charter is framed and ratified, provisional bodies should dissolve and permanent institutions, chosen according to the charter, should assume governance — avoid prolonged interim power concentrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial proclamation asserting 'the law is king' and symbolic rejection of monarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: "let a day be solemnly set apart for proclaiming the charter; let it be brought forth placed on the divine law, the word of God; let a crown be placed thereon... For as in absolute governments the King is law, so in free countries the law ought to be King... But lest any ill use should afterwards arise, let the crown at the conclusion of the ceremony be demolished, and scattered among the people whose right it is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes a public ceremony to proclaim the charter, symbolically place a crown on the law to show that law is sovereign, then destroy the crown to reject monarchy and distribute its remains to the people — a ritual to embody republican principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate, proactive constitution-making to avoid power vacuums and demagogues
rubrics_metrics.description: "A government of our own is our natural right... it is infinitely wiser and safer, to form a constitution of our own in a cool deliberate manner, while we have it in our power, than to trust such an interesting event to time and chance. If we omit it now, some Massanello may hereafter arise..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitution should be framed deliberately and proactively to prevent opportunistic seizure of power and to secure lasting liberty; leaving government formation to chance invites demagogues and tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against patched reconciliation — seek durable independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconciliation now is 'mere patchwork' and 'it is scarcely worth our while to have disputed a matter, which time would have finally redressed, unless we meant to be in earnest;' 'Reconciliation and ruin are nearly related.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial or temporary reconciliation with Britain is evaluated as insufficient and potentially dangerous; only full independence provides a durable and just solution according to the author.
